Operator or trial-sequencing error on day 20; readings are valid but non-random ordering of trials or instrument selection created spurious scatter
Noise floor or measurement resolution changed; day-20 readings are picking up finer instrumental fluctuations not averaged out in baseline
Pendulum_lab and resonator_obs measure a common underlying physical signal with a ~3-day propagation or integration lag

Resonator_obs and pendulum_lab are cross-coupled via a shared environmental path (e.g., mechanical mounting frame, power distribution) with a ~3-day time constant (thermal lag, slow oscillator stabilization)

Trial-sequencing artifact: resonator_obs trials 1–120 were run under different procedural or environmental conditions than later trials; correlation arises from alignment of two independent noise sources by chance, but the specific 3-day lag indicates real but complex causation not yet understood

Instrumental self-similarity: each channel shows periodic echoes of its own past readings (negative or weak positive autocorrelations at lags 3–14 days), suggesting a quasi-periodic environmental or instrumental cycle; the pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_obs correlation is one manifestation of a 3-day-periodic phenomenon affecting the entire settlement
Data entry, event logging, or trial-number transcription error introduced a spurious correlation by misalignment of timestamps or trial indices between pendulum_lab and resonator_obs records

Residual: an unmeasured confound (e.g., a physical phenomenon I have not yet hypothesized, or a failure mode of the instruments themselves that couples to a latent variable) explains the pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_obs correlation and the day-20 scatter in resonators

Shared environmental transient on Day 40 (thermal spike, vibration event, power surge, or electromagnetic interference) simultaneously excited both instruments with high Q-factors, producing coherent scatter; the anomaly is localized in time because the forcing event was brief

Operator or procedural change on Day 40 (e.g., new technician, rushed protocol, or equipment maintenance cycle) altered measurement technique or instrumental setup, increasing noise in both channels without affecting their baseline calibration

The Day 40 scatter is a statistical fluctuation within the normal distribution of post-baseline noise; the anomaly is a false positive arising from multiple-comparisons bias (cherry-picking Day 40 after observing the data)

Instrumental failure or mode transition in one or both devices on Day 40 (e.g., resonator frequency-lock loop lost lock, pendulum magnetic damping circuit developed intermittent contact, or environmental sensor feedback loop saturated)

The previous anomalous pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_obs correlation (r=0.944 at 3-day offset) has resurfaced or is contaminating the Day 40 readings via a delayed feedback mechanism, causing correlated noise in pendulum_lab and resonator_lab (not resonator_obs); this suggests a closed-loop coupling between the two lab instruments

Residual: an unconsidered physical mechanism (e.g., a gravitational wave or cosmic ray burst, a sympathetic resonance from external mechanical vibration, a thermal front propagating through the laboratory at a specific rate, or a calibration standard drift coupled to both instruments via a shared electrical reference)
